source_caption:
The iconic performance that finally won Al Pacino his first Oscar for his role as Lieutenant Colonel Frank Slade in the 1992 film Scent of a Woman.

Al Pacino initially turned down the lead role before his agent convinced him to change his mind. Hollywood heavyweights Jack Nicholson, Harrison Ford, Dustin Hoffman, and Joe Pesci were also considered for the part. Pacino finally credited his agent on a 1994 episode of Inside the Actors Studio for pushing him to take the career-defining role that won him the 1993 Oscar.

source_details.title: Scent of a Woman
source_details.synopsis: Scent of a Woman (Italian: Profumo di donna) is a 1974 commedia all'italiana film directed by Dino Risi, based on Il buio e il miele, a story by Giovanni Arpino. Both Risi and the leading actor Vittorio Gassman won important Italian and French awards. An American remake, Scent of a Woman, was released in 1992.
